verses.1: On one of the Sabbath days, we went deeply onto the tomb, carrying with us the spices that had been prepared in advance.
verses.2: And they found the stone, which was hidden away from the monument.
verses.3: But when you entered, you did not find the body.
verses.4: And it happened that, during their discussion about this matter, two men rushed towards them, with angry expressions on their faces.
verses.5: And because they were in a state of fear, they said to them, “What do you want with the living, along with the dead?”
verses.6: It isn’t like that; he just got up. Remember how he spoke to you when he was still in Galilee.
verses.7: He said to the son of man, “You must be handed over to the hands of sinners, and you must be crucified. On the third day, you will rise again.”
verses.9: And after they were removed from the site, they told all these things to the twelve people, and to everyone else as well.
verses.10: And there were also Magdalene Mary, Joanna, Mary of Jacobus, and the others with them. They said these things to the apostles.
verses.11: And they saw before them those words, just like a scroll with those words written on it. And they believed in them.
verses.12: And Peter stood up and went to the tomb. When he looked around, he saw only empty seats. He returned to himself, marveling at what had happened.
verses.13: And two of them were being taken to a city that was located about sixty stadia away from Jerusalem. The name of that city was Emmaus.
verses.14: And they also discuss with each other all the matters that have occurred.
verses.15: And during their conversations and discussions, Jesus himself would take part in them, guiding them along.
verses.16: And their eyes refused to recognize him.
verses.17: He said to them, “What are these words that you use when traveling together?” They became very ashamed.
verses.18: Then one man named Cleopas replied to him, “You alone live in Jerusalem, and you do not know what is happening there on these days.”
verses.19: And he said to them, “How many?” They replied, “Those related to Jesus Nazarite, who was a powerful prophet in his work and in his words against God and all the people.”
verses.20: So, the high priests and our leaders condemned him to death, and they also crowned him with thorns.
verses.21: We hope that he will indeed be the one who will free Israel from its troubles. But on this third day, he will also leave this place with all these people.
verses.22: But also, some women among us abandoned us. They became traitors to the memory of those who died.
verses.23: And since his body did not seem to be alive, people said that it was just an illusion, like the voices of angels who claimed that he was alive.
verses.24: And some of those who were with us went to the tomb. They found him just as the women said they would find him. But we didn’t see him at all.
verses.25: And he also said to them, “You foolish people, with a slow heart, who believe in everything that the prophets have said.”
verses.26: Isn’t it necessary for Christ to suffer these things and go into His glory?
verses.27: And starting from Moses, and from all the prophets, he taught them everything related to themselves in all the scriptures.
verses.28: They also headed towards the town they were going to. He himself decided to move forward more quickly.
verses.29: And they said to him, “Let him go with us. For it’s already evening, and the day is coming to an end.” So he went with them.
verses.30: And while they were carrying him along, he took the bread, blessed it, and gave it to them.
verses.31: But their eyes became blind, and they could no longer see him. And he became invisible to them.
verses.32: And they said to each other: “Isn’t our heart already like a bird that has been released in our midst, so that it can lead us along the path?”
verses.33: And in that same year, they returned to Jerusalem. There, they found that twelve people had gathered together, along with those who were with them.
verses.34: It is said that the Lord indeed arose and went to Simon.
verses.35: And they also explained what was in the food, and how it was known to them during the meal.
verses.36: While they were speaking these things, he stood in the middle of them.
verses.37: And those who were also curious and interested, believed that it was indeed a spirit.
verses.38: And he said to them, “What are they that cause such trouble in your hearts? And why do they keep causing discord in your hearts?”
verses.39: See my hands and feet, and know that I am indeed that person. Be proud of me, and remember that I do not have a body or bones, as you might think I do.
verses.40: And by saying this, he showed them his hands and feet.
verses.41: And still, they were confused and amazed by this situation. He said to them, “What can we find here?”
verses.42: But those who gave him fish ate it.
verses.43: And when he saw them, he ate them.
verses.44: He said to them, “These are the words I spoke to you when I was still with you. It is necessary that all those laws written in Moses’ law, as well as those of the prophets and psalms, be fulfilled regarding me.”
verses.45: Then he filled their minds with the idea of writing those texts.
verses.46: And he said to them that this is how it is written: to suffer under Christ, and to rise from the dead on the third day.
verses.47: And let there be a call to repentance and forgiveness of sins in all nations, under his name. Let’s begin with Jerusalem.
verses.48: You are witnesses of these things.
verses.49: And now, I will send the message of my father to you. You, on the other hand, must sit down in the city until you are able to act with full authority.
verses.50: He then led them all the way to Bethany. He also tied their hands together.
verses.51: And during their worship, they were separated from him [and he was raised to heaven].
verses.52: And they also, having worshipped him, returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
verses.53: And they were everywhere in the temple, praising the God.
